# What Stripe secret keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Secret is Stripe's word for the three key types that must not be exposed —
# the restricted key, the unrestricted secret key and the organization key —
# and not only for the middle one its table of key types names that way. Its
# guide to protecting keys is titled for managing secret API keys and tells a
# reader to audit for sk_live_ and rk_live_ in one breath; its page on
# organization keys says that all organization API keys are secrets; and the
# page the table stands on says that only publishable keys are safe to expose.
# The publishable key is the fourth type and has a corpus file of its own.
#
# Every key here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is, written out until it is the twenty-four characters the pattern
# holds a body to. That count is a floor and not an abbreviation: a body
# shortened for readability would leave a case holding no key at all. One case
# carries the ninety-nine characters Stripe issues today, to say that the floor
# is not a count.
#
# The two cases under the over-match heading are not keys and nobody issued
# them. What they hold is a snake_case name whose first segment is a key type,
# whose second is a mode and whose third is long enough to be a body, which is
# the whole of what the pattern asks for.
#
# The two cases about the run that readmits a candidate written against a word
# carry no ordered run either: what they turn on is a run's width and not its
# characters, so each is a body of one repeated letter, twenty-one z and
# twenty-two.

patterns: stripe-secret-key

# The kinds of key, which differ in the two letters they open with and in the
# mode written behind them. All three read no in Stripe's safe to expose
# column, which is what puts them under one pattern and puts the publishable
# key under another.

case:     a live secret key in an environment assignment
in:       STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=«stripe-secret-key»

case:     a secret key in the basic auth username a request carries it as
in:       curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges -u sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567:
out:      curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges -u «stripe-secret-key»:

case:     a sandbox secret key
in:       sk_test_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «stripe-secret-key»

case:     a live restricted key
in:       rk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «stripe-secret-key»

case:     a sandbox restricted key
in:       rk_test_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «stripe-secret-key»

case:     a publishable key, which the other half of the format reads
in:       pk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      pk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a restricted key in a bearer token header
in:       Authorization: Bearer rk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      Authorization: Bearer «stripe-secret-key»

# The organization key. Stripe states the prefix sk_org and states that these
# keys support sandboxes and live mode, and states nowhere which of the two
# shapes the mode is written in. Both are read, so a key carrying a mode segment
# of its own and a key carrying none are each redacted whole. What a key in a
# mode Stripe has not written comes to is the last case here, and it is the same
# thing the mode case further down says.

case:     an organization key with no mode segment
in:       sk_org_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «stripe-secret-key»

case:     an organization key with a mode segment of its own
in:       sk_org_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «stripe-secret-key»

case:     an organization key in a sandbox
in:       sk_org_test_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «stripe-secret-key»

case:     an organization key in a mode no Stripe page names
in:       sk_org_prod_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sk_org_prod_0123456789abcdef01234567

# How long a body is, which is the one count this pattern reads. Twenty-four
# characters is the shortest body Stripe has printed in its own documentation,
# and it is read as a floor: the ninety-nine characters Stripe issues today are
# redacted whole, and so would a length neither Stripe nor a ruleset states be.
# What the floor holds back is the placeholder a template carries where a key
# goes, which is the reason it is not lower.
#
# What it leaves over is the key cut short. A line cut to a column limit partway
# through one leaves a prefix and a body too short to be a body, and every
# random character written before the cut comes through in the clear. The two
# cases below are that, and they are here to be looked up rather than arrived
# at.

case:     the length Stripe issues today
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef012
out:      «stripe-secret-key»

case:     a body one character longer than the floor
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567z
out:      «stripe-secret-key»

case:     a key one character short of the floor
in:       STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_0123456789abcdef0123456
out:      STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_0123456789abcdef0123456

case:     a key cut off at its prefix
in:       STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_
out:      STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_

case:     a placeholder where a key goes
in:       STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_yourkey
out:      STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_yourkey

# The mode. It is read as one of the names Stripe writes rather than as any
# lowercase word at all, which is what makes the anchor eight characters instead
# of the three a key type is. What that wagers is a mode Stripe has not written
# yet, and the case below is the one gitleaks reads and no Stripe page names.

case:     a mode no Stripe page names
in:       sk_prod_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sk_prod_0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a key type with no mode behind it
in:       sk_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sk_0123456789abcdef01234567

# The alphabet a body is written in: the letters of both cases and the ten
# digits, which is what every ruleset admits behind a prefix. Neither the
# underscore nor the hyphen is in it, so either of them ends a body where it
# stands and what is left in front of it is too short to be one.

case:     a body written in capitals
in:       sk_live_0123456789ABCDEF01234567
out:      «stripe-secret-key»

case:     an underscore in the body
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef_01234567
out:      sk_live_0123456789abcdef_01234567

case:     a hyphen in the body
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef-01234567
out:      sk_live_0123456789abcdef-01234567

case:     a dot in the body
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef.01234567
out:      sk_live_0123456789abcdef.01234567

# What a key may be written against. The byte in front of a prefix may be no
# letter and no digit, which is a demand few of the patterns here make and the
# Slack one does, for the same reason: both of these key types can close a word
# — task_ ends in sk_ and network_ in rk_. It is not the word boundary a
# regular expression writes: the underscore is admitted, because that is how a
# key reaches a log line from a shell.
#
# Behind the key the redaction reaches to the end of the run, which is the price
# of reading a floor rather than a count. A letter or a digit written straight
# after a key is redacted with it; an underscore, a hyphen, a space or a quote
# ends the run and stays.

case:     a key after an underscore
in:       STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_«stripe-secret-key»

case:     a key after a letter
in:       xsk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      xsk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a key after a digit
in:       1sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      1sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a key at the end of a sentence
in:       the key is sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567.
out:      the key is «stripe-secret-key».

case:     a key inside quotes
in:       export STRIPE_SECRET_KEY="sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567"
out:      export STRIPE_SECRET_KEY="«stripe-secret-key»"

case:     a key before a word
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567suffix
out:      «stripe-secret-key»

case:     a key before an underscore, which ends the run
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567_suffix
out:      «stripe-secret-key»_suffix

case:     a key before a hyphenated word, which ends the run
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567-suffix
out:      «stripe-secret-key»-suffix

# Two keys written together. A key opens only where no letter and no digit
# stands in front of it, and everything a span covers is one or the other but
# for the underscores of the prefix — so a key written against a key would be
# turned away by the body in front of it, were the byte in front the whole of
# the rule. It is not: a candidate opening in front of where the last key ended
# has a whole body of the characters a body is written in behind it, which is a
# key and not a word. The first key's run reaches two characters into the
# second's prefix, so the two spans overlap and a Masker gives back one
# redaction. What stands behind is read and not remembered, so a window reads it
# as the whole text does.

case:     two keys separated by a space
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567 rk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «stripe-secret-key» «stripe-secret-key»

case:     two keys with an underscore between them
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567_rk_test_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «stripe-secret-key»_«stripe-secret-key»

case:     a key written straight onto the end of another
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567pk_test_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «stripe-secret-key»_test_0123456789abcdef01234567

# Three of them, which is where a scan reading the byte in front and nothing
# else loses a key: the first is redacted to the end of its run, which reaches
# two characters into the second's prefix and stops at the underscore behind it,
# and the third opens behind a character of the second's body. The scan reads
# what stands in front of a candidate beside the byte in front for that reason,
# so a key written against a key is located and the run comes out as one
# redaction. builtin_stripe_secret_key.go argues it.

case:     three keys with nothing between them
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «stripe-secret-key»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. A prefix carries two
# underscores, so no base64 payload holds one and no digest does; what is left
# is text somebody wrote — a snake_case name whose first segment is a key type,
# whose second is a mode, and whose third is twenty-four unbroken letters and
# digits.
#
# That is the answer rather than a fault in it: such a name is a key's format
# exactly, so nothing is left in the text to read the two apart by, and the only
# tightening on offer is the count, which the pattern's own file weighs and
# reads as a floor for the reason a wrong count costs a whole credential.

case:     a name whose segments spell a prefix, with a digest behind it
in:       rk_live_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «stripe-secret-key»

case:     the same name at the start of a shell word
in:       cat sk_test_0123456789abcdef01234567.json
out:      cat «stripe-secret-key».json

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The first two are the prefix: read in its
# own case, and written with the underscores Stripe writes rather than the
# hyphens the Anthropic and OpenAI keys carry. Of the last four, the digest
# carries no underscore and so holds no prefix to be found at; no word of prose
# is spelled sk_live_; and the two snake_case names are the ones that carry a
# whole prefix and are turned away by nothing but the letter in front of it —
# task_ closes with a secret key's key type and network_ with a restricted
# key's.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       SK_LIVE_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      SK_LIVE_0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     hyphens where the prefix carries underscores
in:       sk-live-0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sk-live-0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a hexadecimal digest
in:       sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

case:     a snake_case name closing on the secret key type
in:       the task_test_0123456789abcdef01234567 fixture was rebuilt
out:      the task_test_0123456789abcdef01234567 fixture was rebuilt

case:     a snake_case name closing on the restricted key type
in:       network_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      network_live_0123456789abcdef01234567

# A key in the shapes this pattern has nothing to say about the surrounding
# text of, and next to bytes no letter or digit is: a netrc line, a diff, a
# carriage return and japanese text.

case:     a key in a netrc line
in:       machine api.stripe.com login sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567 password x
out:      machine api.stripe.com login «stripe-secret-key» password x

case:     a key on a removed and an added diff line
in:       -STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_0123456789abcdef01234567\n+STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      -STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=«stripe-secret-key»\n+STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=«stripe-secret-key»

case:     a key before a carriage return
in:       STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567\r\n
out:      STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=«stripe-secret-key»\r\n

case:     a key after japanese text
in:       日本語sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      日本語«stripe-secret-key»

case:     a key before japanese text
in:       sk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567日本語
out:      «stripe-secret-key»日本語

# The run of body characters in front of a candidate that readmits it despite
# standing against a word, at the width isStripeKeyBodyRunBefore reads: one
# short of it turns the candidate away exactly as any other word closing on a
# key type does, and at it the candidate is a key.

case:     a run twenty-one characters long closing on the key type
in:       zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzsk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzsk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a run twenty-two characters long readmits the key behind it
in:       zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzsk_live_0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz«stripe-secret-key»
